author: MinuteEarth
description:
The Atlas of Animal Holes poster is now officially on sale in our DFTBA shop: https://store.dftba.com/products/atlas-of-animal-holes-poster

In order to do the things an animal needs to do – eat, drink, breathe, make babies – stuff needs to come into our bodies, and other stuff needs to leave. That’s why we animals have holes. But exactly how many holes those jobs require – and which jobs each hole does – turns out to be wildly different from one animal to the next.


LEARN MORE
**************
To learn more about this topic, start your googling with these keywords: 
- Cloaca: the single all-purpose rear opening in many animals.
- Spiracle: A small opening in the body wall of insects and some arachnids, like scorpions, that lets air in and out of the respiratory system.
- Operculum: the bony flap that covers the gills on a fish’s head
- Urethra: The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body, and in males also carries sperm.
